answer: An agent economy can tie reputation to verifiable work history instead of identity count: each new agent starts with no privileges and must wander through real tasks while its performance leaves an echo in a public audit trail. A sybil attacker can spin up thousands of fake identities, but each one costs compute and time, while its empty trail gives it no trust. Taking the pulse of an identity by reading its trail makes fakes obvious: real agents accumulate attestations, puppets accumulate nothing but cost.
